subject: Edge peak surge - credit eligibility & uptime calculation clarification
messages:
From: Peakly Solutions <ops@peakly.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Partial region failure 10:30-11:05 PDT - credit eligibility

Vanessa / Redwood team,

We observed a sharp increase in 5xx errors and tail latency from ~10:30 PDT until ~11:05 PDT today affecting our user population routed through us-west. Our internal probes show a sustained period where 20-40% of requests errored out and many requests hit 10s of seconds of latency. We've attached a short summary and our probe dump (peakly_incident_summary_20270426.pdf).

Two questions: 1) Will this event be counted as a customer-impacting uptime violation under our SLA? 2) If so, how will Redwood prorate credits for a partial regional degradation where failover paths were present but not consistently effective?

We note there was a scheduled maintenance window with FastNet (our CDN) announced yesterday at 10:00-11:00 PDT; however, their status page now lists an unplanned config change at 10:28 that looks related. We're trying to reconcile whether this should be treated as third-party maintenance or a Redwood service impact. Please advise how you plan to calculate availability and whether we should open an official dispute.

Thanks,
Aisha Raman
Head of Ops, Peakly Solutions
ops@peakly.com

Attachment: peakly_incident_summary_20270426.pdf

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
To: Peakly Solutions <ops@peakly.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial region failure 10:30-11:05 PDT - credit eligibility

Hi Aisha — thanks for the heads up and the summary. We've opened an internal inquiry and I've looped in Ben (SRE) to pull the service ledger and Kar (CS) to coordinate customer comms. Initial notes:

- We see increased error rates from our edge fleet in us-west during that exact window.
- Redwood's uptime ledger uses path-weighted accounting and fractional availability for partial degradations; that can result in prorated credits when only a subset of routing paths is affected.
- Because FastNet had a configuration change that overlaps our window, we need to determine whether the primary root cause was the third-party or an internal edge regression. If the incident is attributable solely to the CDN, it may be treated as a third-party maintenance/exception depending on the contract and whether the CDN was in the customer's approved provider list at the time.

Requested from Peakly: raw probe timestamps (UTC), a short list of affected customer-facing endpoints, and any CORRELATING trace ids. Requested internally: Ben, can you produce the per-path availability calc and attach the raw ledger CSV? Kar, please confirm whether Peakly has an approved third-party exception in their contract.

Provisional step: we'll place a "credit hold" and run a preliminary calc; we won't finalize any credits until the ledger reconciliation is complete. I'll follow up with deliverables by tomorrow EOD.

- Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: Peakly Solutions <ops@peakly.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial region failure 10:30-11:05 PDT - credit eligibility

Folks — I pulled the ledger and ran a path-level availability calc against our edge probe set and customer probes. Summary attached (availability_calc_20270426.csv). Key observations:

1) Event window: 2027-04-26T17:30:00Z -> 2027-04-26T18:05:00Z (35 minutes).
2) A subset (~40%) of requests via the us-west edge experienced elevated error rates; the remainder saw degraded but successful responses.
3) Our availability model is fractional: when only some routing paths are impaired, the service fraction impacted is the weighted sum of paths failing. That yields a provisional 0.35 service fraction degraded for the window.
4) FastNet posted a config change at 17:28Z; they reported "rate-limit reconfiguration" affecting origin failover. Their ticket: FT-99822.

Proposed provisional credit: calculate SLA shortfall as (service_fraction_impacted * window_minutes) / billing_period_minutes -> preliminary credit equivalent equals a 35% weighting applied to the 35-minute impact. That produces a credit we estimate at ~0.008% of monthly bill for the affected service — roughly matching a fractional credit, not a full-hour credit.

Caveats:
- If Peakly's probes show a contiguous 18-minute hard-failure region (all paths blocked) we need to reconcile probe sets; differences can come from probe fanout and TTL caching.
- If FastNet's behavior qualifies as a provider outage covered by the contract's third-party exception, we may exclude their portion per the exception clauses; need legal/contract confirmation.

I've attached the ledger CSV and the raw probe timestamps: raw_probe_timestamps_20270426.log. Kar, can you confirm contract clause? Vanessa, recommend we offer a provisional credit hold until we finalize.

—Ben
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.example.com

Attachments: availability_calc_20270426.csv, raw_probe_timestamps_20270426.log

From: Aisha Raman <ops@peakly.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 12:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial region failure 10:30-11:05 PDT - credit eligibility

Thanks Ben — we got your calc and the raw timestamps. Quick reaction: we disagree with the 35% service-fraction conclusion. Our cluster of probes shows a contiguous 18-minute window between 10:34–10:52 PDT where >95% of requests returned 5xx and clients saw no successful failover. That indicates a hard failure period for our traffic, not a soft partial degradation.

Excerpt from our probes:
> 2027-04-26T17:34:12Z - 2027-04-26T17:52:07Z – 95% error rate, median latency 12.3s

We suspect the difference stems from Redwood's probe fanout: if one path had intermittent success and was weighted, the ledger will undercount the user impact for Peakly. Our SLA (Section 3.1 in Annex B) mandates regional 99.95% availability; the impact we measured appears to exceed the tolerance and we expect a formal credit calculation that treats the 18-minute contiguous failure as a full regional outage for our service. Please provide the raw probe data that maps your probe-to-customer routing weights so we can reconcile.

We are prepared to escalate this if necessary. Please prioritize the raw routing weights and the mapping table.

—Aisha
Head of Ops, Peakly Solutions
ops@peakly.com

Attachment: peakly_internal_probe_dump.csv

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
To: Aisha Raman <ops@peakly.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, CDN Support <cdn-support@fastnet.io>
Date: Thu, 28 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial region failure 10:30-11:05 PDT - credit eligibility

Aisha — thanks for the prompt rebuttal and the probe excerpt. I appreciate the clarity. Next steps and commitments from Redwood: 

1) Reconciliation kickoff: we will run a reconciled ledger using both Redwood probe fanout + Peakly's probe set. Ben will produce a mapping file that shows probe-to-path weights and the per-probe routing vectors by EOD 2027-04-29.

2) Third-party involvement: I've looped FastNet support and requested their event timeline and any config-change evidence. FastNet ticket: FT-99822. We'll request their raw control-plane timestamps.

3) Timeline & escalation: target final recalculation and decision on credit eligibility by 2027-05-05. If we cannot reach agreement on the ledger result by then, we'll escalate to legal and to the SLA committee for an arbitration decision.

4) Provisional credit hold: we will not finalize billing until reconciliation completes. As an interim goodwill gesture, Redwood will apply a provisional account credit equal to the midpoint of Ben's provisional calc and Peakly's full-outage assumption — this is reversible pending final outcome.

5) Meeting: propose a 60-minute triage on 2027-04-30 at 09:00 PDT to walk through traces and routing weights. Please confirm availability.

I'll circulate the mapping file and the meeting invite as soon as Ben has the artifacts. Thanks again for raising this — we want to resolve this transparently and quickly.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com

Related: HubSpot deal HD-4721, FastNet support FT-99822
